```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  comment = NA
)
```

Packages used: sf, ggplot2, classInt, dplyr.

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(classInt)
library(dplyr)
```


Reading GeoJSON:
```{r}
DAs <- st_read('~/Desktop/UBC/GEOS472/geos472-group-map/maps/zonal01.geojson')
```

Examining elevation distribution.
Note that elevation unit is metres above mean sea level.
```{r}
summary(DAs$elevation)
```

Elevation distribution visualised via histogram:
```{r}
ggplot(DAs, aes(x = elevation)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    fill = "steelblue",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of DA Elevations",
    x = "Elevation (metres above mean sea level)",
    y = "Number of Dissemination Areas"
  )
```

Via boxplot:
```{r}
ggplot(DAs, aes(y = elevation)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Elevation",
    y = "Elevation",
    x = ""
  )
```

Calculating natural breaks ranges for 5 classes:
```{r}
nb_DAs <- classIntervals(DAs$elevation, n = 5, style = 'jenks')
nb_DAs$brks
```
Strange...I KNOW parts of Metro Vancouver are below sea level right now, so why is the lowest value 0 and not something negative?
